name: add_fastapi_search_filter
description: Adds category/price/text filtering across repository and router
prompts: The GET /products endpoint currently returns all products. Add optional filtering, spanning both layers: (1) add a search method to ProductRepository in app/repository.py that accepts optional q (case-insensitive substring match on name), category (exact match), and max_price (inclusive upper bound) and returns the matching products; (2) wire those as optional query parameters on GET /products in app/routers/products.py. When no filters are given, all products are returned (order preserved). Combining filters applies them together (AND). Keep the ProductOut response shape.

setup_files.app/schemas.py:
from pydantic import BaseModel


class ProductOut(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    category: str
    price: int
setup_files.app/main.py:
from fastapi import FastAPI

from app.routers import products

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(products.router)

test_setup_files.test_search.py:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)


def ids(resp):
    return sorted(p["id"] for p in resp.json())


# no filters -> everything
assert ids(client.get("/products")) == [1, 2, 3, 4]

# case-insensitive substring on name
assert ids(client.get("/products", params={"q": "steel"})) == [1, 4]

# exact category
assert ids(client.get("/products", params={"category": "garden"})) == [3, 4]

# inclusive max price
assert ids(client.get("/products", params={"max_price": 25})) == [1, 2]

# combined filters are ANDed
assert ids(client.get("/products", params={"category": "garden", "max_price": 35})) == [4]
assert ids(client.get("/products", params={"q": "steel", "max_price": 25})) == [1]

# response shape preserved
one = client.get("/products", params={"q": "hammer"}).json()[0]
assert set(one.keys()) == {"id", "name", "category", "price"}, one
print("PASS")
